requirement_text: UC3M's admission scale runs to 14 points: 'Calificación de Acceso a la Universidad (CAU): hasta 10 puntos' plus 'Mejora de la nota para la admisión: hasta 4 puntos.' For EU/IB/EB/convention-country students, the CAU is the qualification average 'trasladada al sistema español sobre 10 puntos y reflejada en la Acreditación' (issued by UNED).
source_authority_note: uc3m.es is UC3M's own official domain; .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov, so fails the literal gate despite being the university's direct, authoritative admissions page.

requirement_text: For non-EU international students without direct access, UC3M states the formula: 'Nota de Acceso = (0,2xNMB +4) + (0,1xM1) + (0,1xM2) + (0,1xM3) + (0,1xM4)' where NMB is the student's average secondary-school grade and M1-M4 are PCE subject scores (each requiring a minimum of 5). The final admission grade then adds weighted bonus points: 'Nota de Admisión = Nota de Acceso + (M1x0,1 o 0,2) + (M2x0,1 o 0,2)', using the two best-weighted PCE subjects for the target degree.
source_authority_note: UC3M's own official admissions/requirements page; .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov.
researcher_notes: This is the concrete, actionable formula for ORYN's non-EU international users (e.g. a US/AP or Turkish-curriculum student without an EU/IB/convention pathway) applying to UC3M.

requirement_text: For Spanish Bachillerato students, the base grade combines the PAU exam score and Bachillerato average, weighted 'nota de la prueba ponderada a un 40%-60% con la nota media de bachillerato', with up to 4 additional points available from the best two subject grades in the specific admission phase.
source_authority_note: UC3M's own official admissions/requirements page; .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov.
researcher_notes: Provided for completeness/contrast against the international pathway; ORYN's primary international-applicant users will use the UNEDasiss/CAU pathway (see REQ-2026-08-21-1001/1002), not this domestic EvAU/PAU pathway.

requirement_text: UC3M groups UNEDasiss-accredited international applicants into three functional categories with different consequences: applicants from EU/reciprocal-treaty countries can participate in both ordinary and extraordinary allocation rounds, with admission score from PCE grades or recognized coursework plus subject weighting; applicants from non-European countries whose accreditation includes a recognized 'Bachillerato modality' are also eligible for both rounds, combining their bachillerato average with PCE results; applicants whose accreditation does NOT include a bachillerato modality cannot apply in the ordinary round and may only apply in the extraordinary round (late July), and only if vacancies remain after the first allocation.
source_authority_note: UC3M's own official admissions page; .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov.
limitations: The three-category framing here is this research pass's organizing summary of the page's content, not necessarily UC3M's own literal numbered taxonomy — the underlying rules are sourced from the page, but exact official category names were not independently confirmed.
researcher_notes: High-value nuance for ORYN: holding SOME UNEDasiss accreditation is not enough — whether it carries a recognized bachillerato modality changes which admission round a student can compete in at UC3M.

requirement_text: Students able to access UC3M without exams (via direct CAU conversion), provided they meet their home country's own access requirements: EU member-state nationals, International Baccalaureate (IB) holders, European Baccalaureate (EB) holders, and students from countries with bilateral agreements — explicitly named: Colombia, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Liechtenstein, Iceland, Andorra, and China.
source_authority_note: UC3M's own official admissions page; .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov.
researcher_notes: Also independently corroborated on UC3M's estudiantes-internacionales hub page, which lists the same country set for its 'European/Convention System Students' category.

requirement_text: Spanish language accreditation is mandatory for non-Spanish speakers applying to UC3M via the UNED accreditation pathway.
source_authority_note: UC3M's own official admissions page; .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov.
limitations: This specific page confirms the requirement exists but does not restate the exact B2 threshold — the B2 figure itself is corroborated on UCM's equivalent page and in the general Spain-system file (REQ-2026-08-21-0008).

requirement_text: UC3M requires a B2 English level as 'requisito para obtener el título' (a requirement to OBTAIN THE DEGREE) for degree programs with study plans implemented or renewed from 2017 onward. This is explicitly a GRADUATION requirement, not an admission requirement — applicants are NOT required to prove B2 English to be admitted. Admitted students in English-taught or bilingual groups must accredit B2 English during their first year, via an official certificate, a level test administered multiple times yearly, or by passing 60 credits taught in English at UC3M (36 credits in year one suffices to remain in the English-taught group).
source_authority_note: UC3M's own official page on language requirements; .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov.
researcher_notes: IMPORTANT FOR ORYN: do not list this as an admission requirement — it is graduation-stage only. Accepted evidence includes: EOI (Escuela Oficial de Idiomas) 6th year passed, Cambridge First Certificate or higher, IELTS Academic 5.5+, TOEFL iBT 72+, Trinity ISE II+, or full secondary education completed in an English-speaking system.

requirement_text: Each UC3M degree reserves seats outside the general competitive (Grupo 1) pool: '5% para estudiantes con discapacidad' (5% for students with disabilities) and '3% para estudiantes acreditados oficialmente como deportistas de Alto Nivel o de Alto Rendimiento' (3% for officially accredited high-level/high-performance athletes). The page notes published notas de corte 'no se aplican para el alumnado admitido a través de los cupos de reserva de discapacidad o de deportistas de alto nivel.'
source_authority_note: UC3M's own official admissions/requirements page; .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov.
researcher_notes: Relevant context for correctly interpreting the notas de corte recorded above: the published Group 1 cut-off applies to the general competitive pool only, which excludes these reserved-quota seats.

deadline_text_verbatim: Estudiantes de sistemas educativos no españoles: hasta el 6 de julio (hasta las 14:00h) de 2026.
cycle_label: Ordinary preinscripción — foreign education systems, 2026/27 cycle
limitations:
UNEDasiss's own 'fechas_clave' page (https://unedasiss.uned.es/fechas_clave) independently states '7 de julio de 2026' as the general deadline to apply for admission to Spanish public universities for the 2026/2027 cycle — one day LATER than UC3M's own stated 6 July/14:00 cutoff. Both are official pages; not resolved here — see the full side-by-side record in the Spain-system file (DL-2026-08-21-0014). UCM's own page states the identical 6 July/14:00 figure as UC3M, so the discrepancy is specifically UNEDasiss-general vs. both-Madrid-universities, not between UC3M and UCM themselves.

RESOLUTION 2026-08-22 (see docs/research/requirement-conflicts/05-spain-preinscripcion-foreign-systems.md): NOT A CONFLICT — the figures describe different levels of the system. Spanish university admission calendars are set by each autonomous community, not nationally. The Comunidad de Madrid's own access calendar (comunidad.madrid, retrieved 2026-08-22) states for sistemas educativos extranjeros: 'del 5 de junio al 6 de julio a las 14:00' — matching UC3M and UCM exactly, including the 14:00 cut-off. Both belong to the Distrito Unico de Madrid (Alcala, Autonoma, Carlos III, Complutense, Politecnica, Rey Juan Carlos), which admits on one coordinated calendar, so they are two restatements of one source rather than two independent witnesses. UNEDasiss is a UNED credential-accreditation service and owns no region's admission calendar; its '7 de julio' is a general national-level figure. Binding date for UC3M/UCM applicants: 6 July, 14:00. SCOPE: this resolution is specific to Madrid — other autonomous communities run their own calendars and must not inherit either figure. The UC3M/UCM/UNEDasiss pages were NOT re-fetched on 2026-08-22, so retrieved_at is unchanged; the new evidence is the Comunidad de Madrid calendar.
